details: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have intensified, with reports of renewed US attacks on Iran and missile launches from Iran's Lorestan province. This escalation has caused oil prices to surge and fueled a "risk-off" sentiment across global markets, leading investors to seek safe-haven assets. The US has also imposed sanctions targeting Iranian Central Bank crypto wallets. While Bitcoin experienced some dips due to this broader market caution and outflows from exchange-traded funds (ETFs), it also demonstrated some resilience. In contrast, Ethereum has shown an outperformance, supported by decentralized finance (DeFi) and staking activity.
title: Escalating US-Iran Conflict Impacts Markets, Crypto Shows Mixed Response

details: July 1, 2026, marked the official conclusion of the transitional period for the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. This means that full authorization is now mandatory for all crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) serving clients in the EU. Prior to this deadline, thousands of firms operated under fragmented national rules; however, only a small fraction (around 280) have successfully secured the necessary EEA-wide authorization by mid-July. Consequently, many non-compliant firms have either exited the European market, restructured, or are now operating in violation of EU law. Stablecoins like Tether's USDT have been delisted from major regulated EU platforms as they did not meet MiCA's requirements, while USDC is MiCA-authorized.
title: Europe's MiCA Regulation Fully Implemented, Reshaping Crypto Market

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has selected 36 payment service providers (PSPs) from across the euro area to participate in the digital euro pilot, which is expected to commence in the second half of 2027 for a duration of 12 months. This pilot exercise is a crucial step for testing the technical functionality, operational processes, and refining the user experience of the digital euro. The strong market interest, with over 50 applications received, highlights the private sector's engagement in strengthening the European payments landscape.
title: ECB Selects Participants for Digital Euro Pilot

details: Chainlink's technology is being actively integrated into central bank digital currency (CBDC) projects and tokenized asset settlements across multiple countries, including Brazil, Hong Kong, Australia, and the UK, as well as the multi-country mBridge initiative. Its Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) is enabling secure and atomic value transfers between different blockchain networks. These ongoing pilots demonstrate significant progress towards the practical application of blockchain technology in government-backed digital currencies and efficient cross-border payments.
title: Chainlink Advances CBDC and Tokenized Asset Settlements Globally
